newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves additional funds for settler roads.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves additional funds for settler roads.

text.p: The Israeli parliament's finance committee said it approved on Monday an additional 15 million shekels ($4.6 million) to fund cost increases in building roads bypassing Palestinian towns in the West Bank and Gaza.
The roads allow Jewish settlers to bypass Palestinian population centres and are intended to minimise friction between the sides.

The bypass roads plan has stirred opposition from Palestinians, who see it as a guise for increasing areas controlled by Jewish settlers and expanding the amount of Arab land expropriated for Jewish settlements.

The committee's decision to transfer additional funds from a budget reserve fund will allow the plan to be completed during the current fiscal year, the committee said in a statement. The decision does not need further government approval.
Some 130,000 Jewish settlers live amidst nearly two million Palestinians in the territories.

The move comes at a time of heightened tension between Palestinians and Israel. A three-week U.S. effort to broker talks on an Israeli pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron collapsed on Monday with each side blaming the other for the deadlock.
